catalog.summary: Marks matches of a query inside text.

match.input: text, and one of ranges | matcher | query
match.precedence: ranges wins over matcher, which wins over the default matcher
match.empty: a query that is empty or whitespace, or a range set that normalizes to nothing, renders the text alone inside the root
match.normalization: every range set is clipped to the text, ordered, merged where it overlaps or touches, emptied of zero-width entries, and widened to grapheme boundaries
match.reason: The HTML Standard defines mark for exactly this — the term searched for inside a result — and the APG has no pattern for it, so the family is content inside a host rather than a widget. The default matcher is the collator scan createFilter and createRanker already use, so an option that passes the filter shows the mark the filter found; Chakra and Mantine match by a case-insensitive regex, which finds no résumé for resume. Ranges are widened to graphemes because a range cutting a surrogate pair or a combining sequence would put half a character in a mark, and none of the surveyed implementations guards it.

current.attribute: data-current on the match at that index, counting matches only
current.model: none — the family has no keyboard and cannot move the index, so a state model would declare a request nothing can emit; list-item and timeline declare the state the same way
current.reason: react-highlight-words is the one surveyed implementation with an active match (activeIndex); a find bar over a document or a log needs it, and a consumer scrolls to it through the root's ref.

disabled.reason: The mark says why an option is in the list, and saying it in the accent tone on a row that answers nothing puts the loudest thing on the surface on the one option a reader cannot take. The row already carries the state, so the family reads it from above as well as taking it itself.

announcement.decision: mark keeps its semantics and no hidden text is injected
announcement.reason: Most screen readers do not announce mark by default (MDN); a hidden 'highlight start' before every match — the technique MDN documents — would read a five-match option as ten announcements. A consumer that needs the announcement writes the ::before rule in its own scope.

hosts.combobox: the label part holds one root; text, query and locale come from the family that filtered
hosts.select: the same, in the search popup
hosts.listbox: imports nothing; a consumer that marks an option renders the family inside it
hosts.reason: R6: the mark is drawn once. The four hosts rendered the same mark by hand in two bindings each, and each pair could drift from the others.

declined.matchElement: the match is always mark; the element carries the semantics and the forced-colors pair. What react-highlight-words solves with highlightTag this library solves with the highlight tokens.
declined.wholeWord: Chakra's exactMatch alone; a consumer writes it as a matcher over matchRanges and a word-boundary test.
declined.styleObject: docs/component-features.md §2.4: no style object in the contract. The tokens are --slotted-highlight-{background, color, rule-color, tint-opacity, disabled-background, current-background, current-color}.
